chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'adah ibn Sadaqah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), who said:

His father (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Nothing that a believer spends in charity is more beloved to God, the Exalted, than saying the truth when pleased and when angry.'
ai.seo_question: What is more beloved to God than charity according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the virtue of speaking truthfully in both anger and pleasure, noting that this act is dearer to Allah than charitable spending. This comparison underscores the spiritual weight of integrity in emotional extremes, a key theme in Shia ethical teachings on self-mastery and divine favor.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-82 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Mus’adat ibn Sadaqah, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (MGB) , on the authority of his father (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “
Nothing that a believer does is loved by the Honorable the Exalted God more than saying what is right whether he is pleased or angry.”
